name: Xie Yi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2025-2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Xie Yi is the chairman and CEO of Suzhou Tianmai Thermal Technology, a maker of thermal management products including heat pipes and graphite films.
The company went public in Shenzhen in 2024, raising $87 million.
The mogul started his first job when he was only 16, working at a local factory that makes thermal management products.
Xie founded Suzhou Tianmai in 2007 with his wife Shen Fenghua, who is a director at the company.
Nowadays, Suzhou Tianmai supplies to customers including Contemporary Amperex Technology Company (CATL), Huawei and Samsung.

name: Yu Lili
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Yu Lili is a director of electronic products maker Changsha Jingjia Microelectronics. She stepped down as vice chair in August 2024.
Changsha Jingjia Microelectronics went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2016.
Yu's husband Zeng Wanhui chairs Jingjia.

name: Deepak Mehta
forbes_bio: Deepak Mehta is chairman of listed Indian chemicals firm Deepak Nitrite, in which he has a stake.
The company was founded in 1971 by his father Chimanlal Mehta, who died in July 2023.
With a portfolio of 100 products, Deepak Nitrite is a leading producer of phenol and acetone in India.
It has more than 700 customers across the globe.
His son Maulik Mehta, who has a masters degree  in industrial and organizational psychology from Columbia University, is the CEO.

name: Denis Frolov
forbes_bio: Denis Frolov derives his fortune from the Astra Group, a Moscow-listed software company, which went public in 2023 and raised $36 million.
With its Astra Linux software, an operating system, Astra provides software solutions to the Russian government and state-owned companies.
Astra's business has grown following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, providing much-needed digital infrastructure to its government, which was barred from Western technology.
Frolov also has a stake in Sistematika, a Russian IT company with1,500 employees; the company makes up a small part of his wealth.
He is a former executive of Wimm-Bill-Dann, a European dairy producer, which was acquired by PepsiCo in 2010, and has substantial dairy interests in Russia.

name: Hou Juncheng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Hou Juncheng chairs Shanghai-listed Proya Cosmetics,  a supplier of moisturizing and whitening skincare products.
Most of the company's sales come from its "Proya" brand, which are popular among Chinese women between the age of 18 to 24 who reside in small and medium cities.
Hou founded Proya in 2006 as a distributor of local brands such as "Yue Sai" before starting his own product lines.

name: Cyrus Madon
forbes_bio: Cyrus Madon is the executive vice chair of Brookfield Asset Management, a Toronto-based spinoff of Brookfield Corp. which manages $1 trillion in assets.
Madon joined Brookfield in 1998 and was previously the CEO of its private equity business. He remains its executive chair of private equity.
He began his career working in corporate finance at PricewaterhouseCoopers and initially joined Brookfield as CFO of its real estate brokerage business.
Madon also serves on the board of the C.D. Howe Institute, an influential Canadian think tank.

name: Patokh Chodiev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2019); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Eurasian Resources Group (ERG), of which Patokh Chodiev is part owner, got its start investing natural resources in Kazakhstan in the mid-1990s.
With partners Alexander Machkevich and Alijan Ibragimov (both billionaires), he took Eurasian Natural Resources Corp. (ENRC) public in London in 2007.
They delisted ENRC in 2013, after its stock price deflated amid a market downturn, stalled growth and investigative inquiries.
Today, ERG is a diversified natural resources group with production assets and development projects in 14 countries across four continents.
Its activities range from mining and smelting to energy production, logistics and financial services (Kazakhstan's Eurasian Bank is a subsidiary).
forbes_facts: Belgian Chodiev and Israeli Machkevich along with Ibragimov, a native of Uzbekistan who is now a citizen of Kazakhstan, are sometimes referred to as "The Trio."

name: Chang Byung-gyu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Chang Byung-gyu is the chairman of online gaming company Krafton (formerly known as Bluehole), which he founded in 2007.
In 2018, Tencent invested more than $500 million in the company for a 10% stake, catapulting Krafton to unicorn status overnight.
Its shooter game, PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds, broke a world record in 2017 after posting $100 million in pre-release sales in just 79 days.

name: Udo Mueller
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2021-2022)
forbes_bio: Udo Mueller is advertising and marketing firm Stroeer SE's largest single shareholder and the company's co-CEO.
The company dates back to 1963, when it began setting up billboards in Germany.
In 1990, Mueller joined forces with competitor Heinz W. Stroeer to create one of Germany's biggest out-of-home media providers.
Headquartered in Cologne, Stroeer SE went public in 2010. Muller's stake is now just over 22%.
It employs more than 10,000 people in over 100 locations and generates annual revenue of about $2 billion.
forbes_facts: Heinz Stroeer's son Dirk Stroeer, a member of the company's supervisory board, is also a billionaire.
